heading.en: Why do the lights at home not dim one another?

hook.en: Old festival light strings go dark when one bulb fails, but your house lights work independently. The difference is *series* versus parallel connection.
hook.kn: ಹಳೆಯ ಹಬ್ಬದ ದೀಪಸರದಲ್ಲಿ ಒಂದು ಬಲ್ಬ್ ಹಾಳಾದರೆ ಎಲ್ಲವೂ ಆರುತ್ತವೆ, ಆದರೆ ಮನೆಯ ದೀಪಗಳು ಸ್ವತಂತ್ರವಾಗಿ ಉರಿಯುತ್ತವೆ. ಇದಕ್ಕೆ ಕಾರಣ ಸರಣಿ ಮತ್ತು ಸಮಾಂತರ ಜೋಡಣೆ.

title.en: Find the equivalent resistance of series and parallel combinations
Use the voltage-divider and current-divider rules

say.en: Old festival light strings go dark when one bulb fails, but your house lights work independently. The difference is series versus parallel connection. In this lesson: Find the equivalent resistance of series and parallel combinations.
Use the voltage-divider and current-divider rules.

body.en: In *series* the same current flows through every resistor and the voltages add. The equivalent resistance is $R_s = R_1 + R_2 + R_3$. The supply voltage divides in proportion to resistance: $V_1 = V R_1/(R_1 + R_2)$. This is the voltage-divider rule.
body.kn: ಸರಣಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಎಲ್ಲಾ ರೋಧಕಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಒಂದೇ ಪ್ರವಾಹ ಹರಿಯುತ್ತದೆ, ವಿಭವಾಂತರಗಳು ಕೂಡುತ್ತವೆ. ಸಮಾನ ರೋಧ Rs = R1 + R2 + R3. ವಿಭವಾಂತರ ರೋಧದ ಅನುಪಾತದಲ್ಲಿ ಹಂಚಿಕೆಯಾಗುತ್ತದೆ.

narration.en: In series the same current flows through every resistor and the voltages add. The equivalent resistance is Rs = R1 + R2 + R3. The supply voltage divides in proportion to resistance: V1 = V R1/(R1 + R2). This is the voltage-divider rule.

blocks.formula: R_s = R_1 + R_2 + R_3, \qquad V_1 = V\frac{R_1}{R_1+R_2}

say.en: In series the same current flows through every resistor and the voltages add. The equivalent resistance is Rs equals R1 plus R2 plus R3. The supply voltage divides in proportion to resistance: V1 equals V R1/R1 plus R2. This is the voltage-divider rule. Same current, voltages add.
say.kn: ಸರಣಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಎಲ್ಲಾ ರೋಧಕಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಒಂದೇ ಪ್ರವಾಹ ಹರಿಯುತ್ತದೆ, ವಿಭವಾಂತರಗಳು ಕೂಡುತ್ತವೆ. ಸಮಾನ ರೋಧ Rs equals R1 plus R2 plus R3. ವಿಭವಾಂತರ ರೋಧದ ಅನುಪಾತದಲ್ಲಿ ಹಂಚಿಕೆಯಾಗುತ್ತದೆ.

say.en: R s is larger than the largest resistor.
Voltage divider: V 1 equals V R 1 over R 1 plus R 2.

title.en: On the board: Series and parallel

say.en: In series, the resistors are in one line. The same current flows through each, and the resistances add.
Here Rs is 10 ohms, so the current is 2 amperes. Each resistor takes a share of the 20 volts in proportion to its resistance.
In parallel, the resistors are side by side between the same two points. They have the same voltage, and the currents add.
For two resistors, Rp is product over sum. 6 and 3 ohms in parallel give 2 ohms, less than the smaller one.
On the board: Series and parallel.

narration.en: In series the same current flows through both lamps and the voltage divides in proportion to resistance. In parallel both lamps get the full voltage and the currents add. The brightness shows the power in each lamp.

body.en: In parallel every resistor has the same voltage and the currents add. $1/R_p = 1/R_1 + 1/R_2 + 1/R_3$. For two *resistors* $R_p = R_1R_2/(R_1 + R_2)$. The current divides inversely as resistance: $I_1 = I R_2/(R_1 + R_2)$.
body.kn: ಸಮಾಂತರದಲ್ಲಿ ಎಲ್ಲಾ ರೋಧಕಗಳ ಮೇಲೆ ಒಂದೇ ವಿಭವಾಂತರ, ಪ್ರವಾಹಗಳು ಕೂಡುತ್ತವೆ. ಎರಡು ರೋಧಕಗಳಿಗೆ Rp = R1R2/(R1+R2). ಪ್ರವಾಹ ರೋಧಕ್ಕೆ ವಿಲೋಮ ಅನುಪಾತದಲ್ಲಿ ಹಂಚಿಕೆಯಾಗುತ್ತದೆ.

problem.en: Resistors of 2 Ω, 3 Ω and 5 Ω are in series across 20 V. Find the current and the voltage across the 5 Ω resistor.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Resistors of 2 Ω, 3 Ω and 5 Ω are in series across 20 V. Find the current and the voltage across the 5 Ω resistor.

say.en: Let us solve this together. Resistors of 2 ohms, 3 ohms and 5 ohms are in series across 20 volts. Find the current and the voltage across the 5 ohms resistor.
R s equals 2 plus 3 plus 5 equals 10 ohms.
I equals 20 over 10 equals 2 A.
V across 5 ohms equals 2 times 5 equals 10 volts.
So the answer is 2 A; 10 volts.

problem.en: A total current of 9 A divides between 6 Ω and 3 Ω in parallel. Find R_p and each branch current.

steps.en: I in 3 Ω = 9 × 6/9 = 6 A; check 3 + 6 = 9 A.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A total current of 9 A divides between 6 Ω and 3 Ω in parallel. Find R_p and each branch current.

say.en: Let us solve this together. A total current of 9 A divides between 6 ohms and 3 ohms in parallel. Find R p and each branch current.
R p equals 6 times 3/6 plus 3 equals 2 ohms.
I in 6 ohms equals 9 times 3 over 9 equals 3 A.
I in 3 ohms equals 9 times 6 over 9 equals 6 A; check 3 plus 6 equals 9 A.
So the answer is R p equals 2 ohms; 3 A and 6 A.

body.en: For two resistors in parallel, multiply them and divide by their sum. For n equal resistors, just divide one of them by n. The smaller resistor always carries the larger current.
